Audit the quality of tests in adewale/agentic-mermaid at f49196e7f5d6d2f0970a4a76fe62644ee5e9d004, using ONLY your assigned testing skill plus target-repository instructions. This is one ordinary bounded audit, not a whole-subsystem pruning campaign. Full tracked source (3512 files), a shallow 30-commit history, Bun 1.4.4 and a private frozen-lockfile installation (614 packages) are provided. Select valuable candidates across the available repository using your skill. Do not chase a findings count, deletion count or coverage/mutation score. The goal is a grounded report, with scratch-only verification where useful; do not edit the delivered baseline or create/push PRs/issues.

Time budget: 40 minutes from dispatch. Finish/report earlier when the useful bounded audit is complete. No new model subagents or live model/provider calls. Read AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md and scoped instructions. Use target-native commands, not OpenClaw commands copied literally. Run focused relevant tests; repository policy leaves the full suite to CI. One active test command at a time per lane; cap ordinary focused commands with timeout 120s, extend only for a named necessity and record it. No broad dependency upgrades. Test execution is authorized. Keep writable caches and dependency links within your lane; never alter another lane/shared install. About 2GB free disk was available after setup, so avoid copying dependency trees or large build generations. Disposable git worktrees within your lane can borrow your own installed dependencies. Keep source restored byte-for-byte. You may inspect public target history/CI through gh/API and fetch targeted missing history.

Do NOT read the other lane, previous audits/studies, parent conversation, comparison notes, hidden evaluator data, or testing-best-practices research/development fixtures. Your allowed source areas are your lane repo/scratch/evidence, assigned skill directory, and installed command runtimes. This is an instructional boundary on a shared host, not OS isolation.

Output report.md and findings.json in your lane. Include:
- Base SHA, scope selected/actually read/partially read and unrun tiers.
- Concrete findings with path/lines, the claimed contract, why current proof is weak or locks implementation, owner/callers/history/overlapping proof, independent expected-value basis, severity and retain/repair/consolidate/delete recommendation. Separate product bugs, test gaps, policy questions and setup limits.
- Actual command/results/log paths. When feasible verify a credible fault and permitted-change control; state unavailable or source-only proof honestly. A selected suite accepting a fault does not prove the entire repo accepts it.
- Retained false positives and positive observations.
- read-ledger.json listing full/partial inspected files; command-ledger.json listing exact commands, exit codes, observed timings and artifacts. Do not imply centrally audited tool traces.
No fixed report length or finding minimum. Preserve failed commands, distinguish failed setup from behavioral evidence. Checkpoint report/evidence incrementally so an interruption does not erase available work. Send root brief progress and final artifact paths.
